# Talking Head Interview

## Speech-first workflow

- Transcribe before cutting. Correct recognition mistakes without inventing words.
- Work from absolute source timestamps and rebuild subtitles after cutting.
- Remove filler, false starts, long dead air, and accidental repeats while preserving meaningful pauses.
- Build a hook from the strongest existing sentence when requested; do not fabricate a new claim.

## Subtitles

- Keep Chinese captions to roughly 8-16 characters per line and no more than two lines.
- Preserve semantic sentence boundaries. Do not split a phrase only to hit a line length.
- Keep captions inside the video safe area and away from faces, lower thirds, and platform controls.

## Picture rhythm

- Do not cut on every sentence. Use a stable talking-head shot with punch-ins at key points.
- Add B-roll or relevant photos when they clarify a claim, not merely to hide every jump.
- A punch-in should be subtle and purposeful, generally about 1.03-1.10 scale.
- Use chapter or topic titles for structure, not repeated subtitles of the spoken line.

## Verification

- Does every retained sentence still have its context?
- Are captions synchronized and readable?
- Does B-roll support the spoken claim?
- Are names, titles, numbers, and claims traceable to the source?
